rationale: Interpreted the new receipt, which answers both halves of the store-failure question for the shape it measures and turns the lead from a source account into a witnessed one. In the injected case the conflicting append left the follower with an in-memory last index of 3 while its store held only index 1 and no longer held index 2, and the handler answered that RPC with Success false and LastLog 3; the whole-log re-append that would have repaired it was then rejected as well, with the store still at index 1. The control case, identical in every request and setting except that the store did not fail, accepted both appends and ended with the store at index 3. I recorded the measured divergence and rejection as a Fact with the receipt's indices, rewrote the question's account around the witness with the experiment id and its executions, and re-pointed the discriminator at what the receipt does not cover - a live leader producing the retry sequence, and the stale index as it is used in the follower's own vote responses.

investigations.discriminator: A live leader replicating to a follower whose store failed inside the truncation window: the leader's nextIndex for that peer over the following interval and whether its rejections walk it down to the start of the log, whether the follower then accepts anything before a snapshot is installed, and the last log term and index the follower reports in its own vote responses while the state persists.

interpretations.rationale: The question has two halves and the execution answers both for the sequence it exercises. After the conflicting append with the store failure armed (receipt bd46b877825a4476b23bcc394778c324, injected case, conflict event index 1) the follower's own last log index was 3 while its store's last index was 1 and index 2 was no longer stored, and the handler answered that RPC with Success false, the stale LastLog of 3 and no rpc error, because it had deleted the suffix, failed to store the replacement and returned before setLastLog. The repair half is the decisive one: the next AppendEntries carried the whole log from index 1, exactly the request whose rejection walks a leader's nextIndex back to the start of its log, and the follower rejected it too (index 2, Success false, store still at index 1), because the conflict loop treats index 2 as present while the stale in-memory last index stands at 3 and then fails to read it from the store. The control case, same requests and same settings with the store failure not armed, accepted both appends and ended with the store at index 3 (indices 4 and 5), so the rejection is caused by the failure and not by the request sequence. What is measured is therefore the stale index, the response the leader receives and the refusal of an ordinary append that would have restored consistency; what remains inferred from the source is that a leader's rejections actually walk nextIndex down to that request, and that only the snapshot path or a restart ends the state, since the receipt sends those requests itself rather than through a live leader replicating to this follower.
counterevidence: The trigger is a store error on one RPC, and the library's leader path treats the same error as a reason to step down and to fail the caller, so a store error may be intended as a condition that takes a node out of service rather than one a follower must survive in place.

The repair request is supplied by the probe rather than produced by a live leader in this receipt, so what is witnessed is that the follower refuses that request, not that a cluster's leader reaches it on its own.
The state need not be permanent: the snapshot path fires once the leader's log no longer holds the follower's nextIndex, and a restart rebuilds the in-memory last log from the store.

The follower keeps answering, its rejections carry the leader's term, and it stays outside the leader's commitment accounting either way, so no committed entry of the cluster is decided by the stale index.
limitations: One execution of six events, two cases and one request shape each; the rejection was uniform but the probe does not vary the failure point, the number of retries, or the timeout settings, which were two seconds for heartbeat, election and lease.

The account depends on a supplied fault - a store whose StoreLogs returns an injected error for the append that follows a truncation in the same RPC - and says nothing about torn writes, a lost acknowledged write, or a monotonic store.

The contract is disputed in the counterevidence above: the same store error leads the leader path to step down, so an operator may be expected to restart the node instead of relying on in-place repair.
The effect of the stale index on the follower's own vote responses is still unmeasured, as is the live-leader retry sequence that the source says produces the repair request.

knowledge.assertion: The aborts that can follow a suffix deletion in the same RPC return without advancing the in-memory last log, so the follower keeps an index its store has lost.

knowledge.statement: A follower whose AppendEntries handler deletes a conflicting suffix and then fails to store the replacement keeps an in-memory last log index that its store no longer holds, answers that RPC with Success false and that stale index, and refuses a later AppendEntries carrying the whole log, while the same sequence without the store failure is accepted. In the executed probe the injected case ended the conflicting append with in-memory last index 3 against a store whose last index was 1 and which no longer held index 2, and the whole-log re-append was rejected with the store still at index 1; the control case ended both appends with the store at index 3 and Success true.
knowledge.conditions: One in-process raft node with an in-memory log store wrapped by a store that fails exactly one StoreLogs call, a transport used to deliver three AppendEntries requests directly to the node's handler (baseline entries 1-3 at term 1, conflicting entries 2-3 at term 2, then entries 1-3 again), two-second heartbeat, election and lease timeouts, no live leader and no snapshot activity.
